sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Home page copy and links
sections.what: Checks the home page has no statistics, illustrative wording or athlete names, shows the expected AI analyst cards and in-development notice, and that every internal link works.
sections.why: Keeps the landing copy aligned with what the app actually ships and stops dead links.
sections.watch_out: The no-digits rule is strict, so any legitimate number such as a year or version will fail it.

summary: Browser tests of the home page that check its copy contains no statistics, illustrative data or athlete names, and that every link on it leads to a working page.
purpose: Keeps the home page honest about what ships and makes sure its calls to action lead somewhere real.
why: Making claims or using real athlete names on the landing page could mislead users or raise legal issues, and broken links waste visitors' time.
how: The first test reads the main text, removes the word Formula 1, and expects no line containing digits apart from list markers. It also checks for words like illustrative or simulated and for a set of athlete and codename words. It expects five AI analyst cards and two specific headings and messages. The second test collects all internal links in the header and main area and checks each returns a successful status.
inputs: The home page and its links.
outputs: Pass or fail for copy rules and for link health.
risks: Any legitimate number on the page, such as a year, will fail the statistics check. The athlete list is hard-coded.
debug: Read the reported line to see which number or word triggered the failure. For broken links, request that address directly to see the status.
